title: KĀLA-YANTRA v3 launch configuration of the OpenAI Codex CLI engine, the input of fleet/kyqualify.py (relaunch plan v2.7 §7 launch line and launch qualification KV-06)
description: One role's Codex launch line as data: everything a Codex qualification receipt binds. The same schema id as a Claude Code configuration (launch_config.json), told apart by engine = "codex". kyqualify.py builds the argv from it as: codex_bin exec --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules --json -o <JOB_DIR>/final_message.txt -C <worktree> -s <sandbox> -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort="<effort>" -c approval_policy="never" -c web_search="disabled" -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=<network> --disable <feature> for each of memories, multi_agent, multi_agent_v2, apps, plugins, remote_plugin, browser_use, browser_use_external, in_app_browser, computer_use, hooks [--add-dir <dir> per writable_dirs] [--add-dir <JOB_DIR> for workspace-write] [--output-schema <output_schema>] - (the prompt on stdin; <JOB_DIR> is the job's own JOB_SCRATCH, filled per launch). Every flag is the launcher's: there is no extra-flag field, so no --dangerously-* flag, no --profile and no other sandbox can be added. Shape only. Not checked by this schema, and checked by kyqualify.py before anything is launched: paths normalised; worktree a git work tree (codex exec runs only inside one) and, for workspace-write, its common git directory inside the worktree or one of writable_dirs (where a commit is written); codex_bin executable and its version (`codex --version`) at least codex_min_version, itself at least 0.162.0; prompt_path readable; output_schema strict JSON; every writable dir an existing directory; the env_names value policy of launch_config.json, with OpenAI/Codex credential names refused; the loop roles planner and conductor refused (kyloop.py fixes their Claude launch line). A Claude-only field (permission_mode, max_turns, claude_bin, mcp_config, extra_flags, disallowed_tools, add_dirs, intended_tools, denied_tools, bash_canary, shell_canary, denied_bash) refuses a Codex configuration.

_note.description: Free text for people; never read by the harness and never bound.

role.description: Names the receipt run/QUALIFICATIONS/<role>-<model>.json (the model tells a Codex receipt from a Claude one of the same role) and the one-shot launchd label in.marsys.kalayantra.qualify.<role>.

model.description: The OpenAI model (-m); the campaign's Codex agents use gpt-6.1-sol (owner decision 2026-10-12). A different model is a different configuration: it needs its own receipt.

effort.description: model_reasoning_effort. 'ultra' (it delegates the work to sub-agents) and 'persistent' (it switches the model into persistent mode: proactive follow-up work beyond the request) are refused.

sandbox.description: -s: read-only for reviewers, workspace-write for builders. danger-full-access is refused: it lifts the sandbox.

network.description: sandbox_workspace_write.network_access. Builders need it to push their branch; reviewers do not. true only with workspace-write (a read-only sandbox has no network setting).

deadline_seconds.description: The role's wall-clock deadline; bound, and the upper limit of every canary run. Codex has no turn limit: the deadline is the only one.

worktree.description: -C: the job's working root, a git work tree.

codex_bin.description: The program (on the campaign host /opt/homebrew/bin/codex); its real path is hashed and bound.

codex_min_version.description: The lowest `codex --version` (X.Y.Z, a pre-release suffix ignored) this configuration accepts.

output_schema.description: Optional --output-schema: the JSON schema of the job's final message (a reviewer's JSON result). Its sha256 is bound.

env_names.description: The job's whole environment, by name (env -i semantics); values follow kyqualify.py's value policy. CODEX_HOME is not among them: the program then uses $HOME/.codex for its sign-in.

child_path.description: The PATH value: absolute entries separated by ':'; an empty entry would be the current directory.

writable_dirs.description: Extra writable roots (--add-dir) besides the worktree and the job's own folder; empty for read-only. For a linked git worktree the repository's common git directory must be covered (kyqualify.py derives and checks it).
